newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee reports 47 percent rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee reports 47 percent rise in profits.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp. on Tuesday reported a 47 percent increase in first-quarter profits that surpassed Wall Street predictions and cited strong crude oil and natural gas prices.
The Oklahoma City-based energy and chemical company posted earnings of $70.2 million, or $1.45 per share, compared with $47.9 million, or 94 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The consensus industry analyst forecast had put earnings at $1.28 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst predictions.
Kerr-McGee had consolidated sales of $468 million, up 3 percent from $454.8 million in 1996.
"Higher first-quarter 1997 operating profit resulted primarily from strong crude oil and natural gas sales prices," company Chairman Luke Corbett said in a statement.
However, those gains were partly offset by lower chemical and coal profits, the company said.
Kerr-McGee's operating profit from oil and gas explorationand production hit $68 million, a 97 percent increase from last year's $34.6 million.
Operating profit from chemicals, meanwhile, dropped 50 percent to $15.2 million from $30.6 million, mainly from lower titanium dioxide prices and higher production costs, the company said.
The coal business's operating profit fell 15 percent to $15.3 million from $18 million due to lower sales prices and higher production costs at Kerr-McGee's Galatia mine in Illinois.
Kerr-McGee stock rose $1.25 to $59.625 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon.
